title: Operator decision sandbox and simulated fallback library
author: Samantha Chen
content:
Overview

This page documents the Operator Decision Sandbox (ODS): a curated library of deterministic, repeatable simulations and fallback recipes platform operators can run in the staging playground to validate choices before applying them in production. The goal is to reduce cognitive load, speed triage, and improve judgement consistency when services degrade.

Audience and scope

- Primary audience: platform operators, SREs, oncall engineers, and operator mentors.
- Scope: simulated failure modes for the inference stack (routing, batching, allocator, and cache), SLO-sensitive decision rules, and a canonical set of operator actions with expected outcomes. This does NOT replace the primary runbooks; it augments them with reproducible testcases to validate operator decisions.

Motivation

Operators faced three common failure patterns during Q4 2025: ambiguous alert context, conflicting mitigation options (evict vs. throttle vs. swap), and slow rollback verification. The sandbox provides:

- Repeatable scenarios to rehearse decisions with real telemetry slices.
- A decision lattice mapping actions -> risk profile -> rollback path.

How the sandbox is organized

Sections:
1) Simulation catalog (deterministic scripts + inputs)
2) Decision lattice (operator actions with safety gates)
3) Run instructions and verification checklist
4) Scenario matrix (table) with SLO impact estimates
5) Post-simulation retrospective template

1) Simulation catalog (examples)

Each simulation is stored in the operator-sandbox git repo under ops-sims/ and has: metadata.yaml, traffic-replay.tar.gz, expected-metrics.json, and a control script. Example entries below.

- sim: degraded-routing-congestion-v2
  - trigger: synthetic tenant traffic spike replay
  - primary_services: inference-router, allocator, request-queue
  - control: scripts/degraded-routing/run.sh --replay ops-sims/degraded-routing/traffic-replay.tar.gz --seed 20251112
  - expected-metrics.json snippet: {"router_5xx_rate": ">=0.5%", "avg_p95_latency_ms": ">=1200"}

- sim: kvcache-corruption-slow-read
  - trigger: injected partial header corruption in kv-prefix-cache waterline
  - primary_services: kv-prefix-cache, batching-service, fallback-store
  - control: scripts/kvcache-corrupt/run.sh --inject-corrupt --cohort small
  - expected outcome: graceful fallback to prefix-miss paths, small increase in egress cost, no model swap required

- sim: quantization-regression-high-bytes
  - trigger: deployed quantized model variant with broken kernel path causing token blowup
  - primary_services: serving-runtime, kernel-switcher, telemetry-ingest
  - control: scripts/quant-regression/run.sh --variant q4-8bit --replay sample-chatset.tar.gz
  - expected outcome: increased token emission per prompt, token-cost SLO burn >= 3x baseline

2) Decision lattice (operator actions and safety gates)

The lattice maps common operator actions to risk and rollback windows. Operators should consult the lattice before escalating. Example (short form):

- Action: soft-throttle tenant (apply 20% throttle)
  - Risk: medium (can cause request backlog)
  - Safe-to-apply guard: dynamic-queue-depth < 90%
  - Verify: deployment-level p95 latency improves in 2 windows (10m, 30m)
  - Rollback: remove throttle gradually over 60 minutes with telemetry gating

- Action: swap model -> smaller variant (model-swap to f32-lite)
  - Risk: high (quality regression risk)
  - Safe-to-apply guard: canary traffic < 1% of total and canary-eval suite passes basic semantics
  - Verify: quality metric (BLEU/ROUGE/LLM-specific eval) within 10% of baseline after 15 minutes
  - Rollback: immediate fallback to pinned baseline variant with warmup prefetch

- Action: evict warmset shard from GPU pool
  - Risk: low-to-medium (cold starts possible)
  - Guard: estimated cold-start penalty < 200ms median for critical path
  - Verify: token latency for prewarmed cohort returns to baseline within 20m

3) Run instructions (operator quick-start)

Prerequisites: operator-sandbox access, kubectl to sandbox cluster, staging telemetry credentials, 2GB free local disk for replay artifacts.

Basic flow:
1. Pick scenario from Simulation catalog.
2. Create a reproducible incident branch in the sandbox: git checkout -b ops-sim/<scenario>/<your-initials>.
3. Run the control script in a Tmux session: ./scripts/<scenario>/run.sh --seed <seed> --duration <minutes>
4. Open dashboard template: dashboards/ops-sim-<scenario>.json in the sandbox Grafana namespace.
5. Execute operator action(s) from the lattice while recording timestamps.
6. Validate expected-metrics.json assertions locally: python3 tools/validate_metrics.py --expected sims/<scenario>/expected-metrics.json --window 10m
7. Write a short retrospective (section below) and push results to the operator-sandbox repo.

Commands (examples):

# start sim in background
./scripts/degraded-routing/run.sh --replay ops-sims/degraded-routing/traffic-replay.tar.gz --seed 20251112 &

# validate metrics
python3 tools/validate_metrics.py --expected ops-sims/degraded-routing/expected-metrics.json --prom-url https://staging-prom.redwood.internal --window 10m

4) Scenario matrix (quick reference table)

Name | Trigger | Primary metrics to monitor | Fast mitigation | Risk | Time-to-verify
-----|---------|----------------------------|-----------------|------|----------------
Degraded routing congestion | traffic spike replay | router_5xx_rate, p95_latency_ms, pending_queue_depth | soft-throttle tenant | medium | 30m
KV cache corruption (partial) | injected corruption | prefix_miss_rate, cache_hit_ratio, model_tokens_per_request | fallback-to-store, increase cache read timeout | medium-low | 20m
Quantization regression | new quantized kernel rollout | tokens/generated_per_prompt, token_cost_rate | immediate model-swap to f32-lite canary | high | 15m
Allocator starvation | sustained allocation failures | allocator_failure_rate, queue_retries, preempt_count | enable-burst-pool, reduce-fair-share | high | 45m

(For a machine-readable CSV, see ops-sims/scenario-matrix.csv in the sandbox repo.)

5) Expected SLO impact estimations

We provide conservative SLO impact ranges operators should use when communicating with incident leads. These are historical medians with a safety buffer.

- Minor: <1% SLO burn in 1 hour
- Moderate: 1%–5% SLO burn in 1 hour
- Severe: >5% SLO burn in 30 minutes

6) Operator runbook snippet (triage flow)

1) Ingest alert into incident lead channel and open ODS ticket.
2) Map alert to nearest sandbox scenario (use tags in the alert payload).
3) Run the scenario in sandbox and reproduce the metric deltas.
4) Walk through the lattice: pick the lowest-risk action whose guard conditions are satisfied.
5) Apply action with telemetry gates and defined rollback window.
6) Monitor for verification windows; if verification fails, escalate to oncall engineering and apply rollback immediately.
7) Document decisions and publish a one-paragraph retrospective.

7) Verification checklist (copy into incident notes)

- [ ] Scenario replayed in sandbox with matching delta signature
- [ ] Safety guard for chosen action validated
- [ ] Action applied with clear timestamps and operator identity
- [ ] Verification metrics improved in the expected direction
- [ ] Rollback path staged and tested (dry-run if possible)
- [ ] Postmortem ticket created with preliminary hypothesis

8) Post-simulation retrospective template

Use this template when pushing results back to ops-sims/results/:
- Simulation name:
- Run by (name/team):
- Date/time/stage seed:
- Short description of observed deltas:
- Actions tested (include CLI commands and timestamps):
- Outcome summary (metrics before/after):
- Recommendations (do not apply to prod unless reviewed):
- Confidence level (low/medium/high):

9) Ownership and maintenance

- Owners: eng-platform/operator-experience (primary), eng-platform/observability (secondary)
- Review cadence: quarterly scenario validation before high-traffic seasons
- How to propose new scenario: open PR to ops-sims/catalog with metadata.yaml, traffic-replay, expected-metrics.json, and a run script; include a short justification and owner on the PR.

10) Example metadata.yaml (required fields)

---
name: degraded-routing-congestion-v2
owner: eng-platform/operator-experience
contact: ops-oncall@redwood.com
severity_estimate: moderate
primary_services: ["inference-router","allocator","request-queue"]
replay_artifact: degraded-routing/traffic-replay.tar.gz
expected_metrics: degraded-routing/expected-metrics.json
---

Appendix A — Dashboard template notes

- Each scenario must include a Grafana template with: 1) timeline view of the key metrics, 2) heatmap of per-tenant p95 latencies, 3) a token-cost delta panel, 4) an annotation layer for operator action timestamps.
- Template filename convention: dashboards/ops-sim-<scenario>-template.json

Appendix B — Safety principles (short)

1) Prefer reversible, low-latency mitigations first.
2) Always stage high-risk changes under canary traffic.
3) Record operator actions with timestamps and reason.
4) Favor telemetry gates for both apply and rollback.

Appendix C — Glossary

- ODS: Operator Decision Sandbox
- Guard: a boolean condition derived from telemetry that must be true before applying an action
- Warmset: subset of prewarmed model shards assigned to keep latency low
